title: Waymo to launch first phase of driverless taxi testing in Toronto with service expected in 2028
key_facts: Waymo, owned by Google parent Alphabet, said in a news release on Friday 16 Oct 2026 that its driverless ride-hailing service is expected to launch in Toronto in 2028.

Toronto residents may start to see Waymo vehicles "in the coming days" as a first testing phase begins; the phase starts with mapping local streets and testing with trained specialists behind the wheel.
Waymo says its service has been approved to take part in Ontario's automated vehicle pilot program, launched 10 years ago; a 2019 change allows driverless vehicles under certain conditions.
Waymo already runs all-electric Jaguar I-PACE vehicles in 10 major US markets; its Toronto partner is Element Fleet Management, which will provide maintenance, customer service and other support.
Co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana said Waymo looks forward to partnering with businesses and communities in Toronto.

Mayor Olivia Chow said her biggest concern is safety and that the permitting law is the province's, not the city's; Uber Canada policy head Laura Miller asked for clear safety standards and preparation "for the impact on workers".
Sidney Givigi, a robotics and machine learning professor at Queen's University, warned that snow can block the sensors and asked what happens on ice or in a blizzard.
City staff earlier criticized another firm's test cars (Magna International) in a letter to the province: they could not make right turns at red lights and sometimes rebooted in traffic.
quote_evidence: Autonomous vehicle operator Waymo is officially coming to Canada with the driverless ride-hailing service expected to launch in Toronto in 2028, the company says.
Mayor Olivia Chow said her biggest concern is about the safety of Torontonians and ensuring that autonomous vehicles are held to the highest standards.
"All the sensors can get occluded by snow," Givigi said, "which is something that they don't have in California.
why_it_matters_hint: Waymo has named Canada's largest city as its first Canadian market, with a 2028 target, while drivers' jobs and winter performance remain open questions.
